tests: [console.test] console should have location when fetch fails
reason: Puppeteer skips these under WebDriver BiDi: BiDi has no counterpart of Chromium's Log domain, so the browser's own console entries for a blocked or failed fetch aren't reported

tests: [console.test] console should not dispose handles when page has listeners
reason: Reads a console message's arguments as values or handles, with their count, `jsonValue`, and properties. A ConsoleMessage carries the formatted text, level, and location, not its arguments

tests: [console.test] console should have location and stack trace for console API calls
[console.test] console should have scriptId in stack trace for eval console API calls
reason: Reads the message's stack trace, and a `scriptId` on the location and each frame. A ConsoleMessage doesn't carry a stack trace; its location is one frame's URL, line, and column

tests: [console.test] console should report the originating frame and page for iframe logs
reason: Reads the frame that wrote the message (`message.frame()`), which for an iframe's log is the iframe, not the main frame. A ConsoleMessage's origin is a page, named by its main frame's navigable, or a worker's realm: it doesn't name the frame. The row is the nearest: it lists `ConsoleMessage.page` as missing, and `frame` has none

tests: [console.test] console should not throw when there are console messages in detached iframes
reason: Strider refuses popups.opener on stock WebKit: stock WebKit) (stock WebKit names no page's opener: a page another opens is reported as the browser's

tests: [console.test] console should include null and undefined in text()
[console.test] console should have location when fetch fails
reason: Browser-generated console messages (CORS errors, failed loads) are never reported on Chromium or WebKit

tests: [console.test] console should not fail for window object
reason: ConsoleMessage.text has no value preview, so objects, arrays, and windows read as the browser's class name, differently per browser

tests: [console.test] console should work for Error instances
reason: ConsoleMessage.text for an Error argument is each browser's own description: Chromium appends the stack, the others the whole message

tests: [console.test] console should return the first line of the error message in text()
reason: ConsoleMessage.text for an Error argument is each browser's own description: Chromium appends the stack, the others the whole message

tests: [console.test] console should work for different console API calls with timing functions
[console.test] console should work for different console API calls with group functions
reason: ConsoleMessage has no type for console.dir, trace, group, groupEnd, or timeEnd: they all read as 'log' (or 'debug')
